title: Part One
html:
Benediction. The Pancha-tattva. Navadvipa. The succession from Madhva. Mahaprabhu's relatives and teachers (verses 1–57)

Mangalacharana

1He who once, in the land of Vrindavana — the concentrated essence of being, consciousness and bliss, an abode of dark splendour — danced with golden-limbed maidens equal to Him in lustre; and who, perhaps because of their eternal and ever tighter embraces, Himself became golden — that Gauranga, who dwells in Navadvipa, be glorious!

2We bow to the beloved, tender-hearted associates of this Lord — Advaita and the others, who destroy the floods of the world's sins; and we praise also those — Svarupa and the rest — who are equal to them in love, equal in qualities and equal in compassion, full of rasa and sweetness.

3We bow to our guru named Srinatha,1 a moon in the line of the brahmanas, a jewelled ornament of the earth as it were, dear to the Lord: having tasted the pure, unalloyed talks of the secret pastimes of Vrindavana that pour from his lips, no one in the world delights in anything else.

4With supreme devotion I worship my father, Sri Shivananda, the lamp of the Sena family, foremost among the associates of Mahaprabhu.

The sources of this book

5The famous associates of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, and those of the great Nityananda and Advaita too, and some of the former names of the cowherds which the first sages — Svarupa and others — pointed out each in his own book: having studied these, and having heard others from the lips of saints living in Mathura, in Odra (Orissa) and in Gauda, having considered them with my own understanding, and being repeatedly asked by some — I, named Sri Paramananda Dasa, carrying out the command given to me, write them down.

The beginning

6As once Krishnachandra, being fivefold in nature (pancha-tattva), became manifest in the world, so Gaura too became manifest.

7The Truth joined with what is non-different from Itself is here called the pancha-tattva. Otherwise, were there no such connection, the truths would be a set of four.2

8What is different from Him should here be understood as non-different from Him, for Krishna by His own will, by His own potency, has assumed such a form.

9Therefore the feet of Svarupa3 in the Tattva-nirupana ("Description of the Truth") have shown the fivefoldness of the one Truth according to the difference of its designations:

10"I bow to Krishna, fivefold in nature: the devotee in form, the devotee in essence, the incarnation of the devotee, the one called a devotee, and the potency of the devotee."

11The meaning of this, as he explained it, I set down in brief. Gaurachandra is "the devotee in form," for He is the son of Nanda. Nityananda, who in Vraja is Sri Halayudha,4 is "the devotee in essence." Advaita Acharya, who is Sri Sadashiva, is "the incarnation of the devotee." Srivasa and the others are "those called devotees," for they have the form of devotees. And "the potency of the devotee" is the foremost of brahmanas, Sri Gadadhara Pandita.

12Srimad Vishvambhara, Advaita and Nityananda Avadhuta — these three are here to be understood as the Vigrahas and as the Prabhus. The one Mahaprabhu is Sri Chaitanya, the ocean of mercy; the two Prabhus are the glorious Nityananda and Advaita, the great-souled. They are the Gosvamis and the Vigrahas; and together with the brahmana Gadadhara and Srinivasa Pandita they constitute the pancha-tattva.

13As the lotus feet of Gosvami Sri Svarupa have said: "Here three are to be known as the Vigrahas, and these same three are the Prabhus; of them one is acknowledged by the saints as Mahaprabhu, and two as Prabhus."

14Among their circles of associates, celebrated as the mahantas, all the associates of Nityananda are gopalas — cowherd boys in cowherd dress; and by their connection and closeness with them, others are the best of the upa-gopalas.5

15Those of them who sported in glorious Navadvipa near Vishvambhara are to be known as the very greatest Vaishnavas (mahattama).

16Those who became famous in Nilachala are to be known as great (mahattara). Those with whom Mahaprabhu kept company on His journeys to the south and in other directions are also to be regarded as mahantas; the rest are to be known according to their own merit.

17Therefore the feet of Svarupa said in the Gaura-nirupana ("Description of Gaura"): "Those who became famous as the greatest through their connection with the pancha-tattva are the mahanta-gopalas; these words indicate pre-eminence of place and so on."

Navadvipa

18That which the knowers of rasa call Sri Vrindavana, which the learned call Goloka, which some call Shvetadvipa, and others still the supreme Paravyoma — that is Navadvipa, whose greatness is supremely wonderful; may it be glorious!

19There Nrihari,6 taking the name Vishvambhara, made His dwelling; and, drawn by His deeds, all the great souls came to dwell there too. With them the great pastime (lila) of Hari took place there, befitting His form, in which even the mind of the whole world became immersed in supreme bliss.

20He who in the Satya age assumed a white colour and was called Sri Shukla; who in the Treta age, assuming a red colour, was rightly called Makha, the enjoyer of sacrifices; who in the Dvapara age was dark, assuming a dark colour — this very Gaura-moon shines now in the age of Kali, manifesting as the incarnation of the Holy Name.

The succession

21In the age of Kali four sampradayas appeared, called those of Sri, of Brahma, of Rudra and of Sanaka, as is recorded in the Padma Purana: "Therefore in the age of Kali there will be four sampradayas — the Vaishnavas of Sri, Brahma, Rudra and Sanaka, purifiers of the earth."

22Of these, the sampradaya of Madhva is here described in detail. The disciple of the Lord of Paravyoma was Brahma, the lord of the world. His disciple was Narada, and Vyasa became Narada's disciple. Shuka became the disciple of Vyasa, having given up (dry) knowledge. His disciples and grand-disciples are many on the earth. From Vyasa the renowned Madhvacharya received initiation into the mantra of Krishna. Having divided (examined) the Vedas, he composed the compendium Shatadushani,7 in which Brahman with qualities is established as distinct from Brahman without qualities. His disciple was the venerable Padmanabhacharya; his disciple was Narahari, and his disciple the brahmana Madhava. His disciple was Akshobhya, whose disciple was Jayatirtha; his disciple was Jnanasindhu, whose disciple was Mahanidhi; his disciple was Vidyanidhi, whose servant was Rajendra; his disciple was the sage Jayadharma, from whose circle came Srimad Vishnupuri, the author of the Bhakti-ratnavali. The disciple of Jayadharma was Purushottama, [and after him] Brahmanya; his disciple was Vyasatirtha, who composed the Vishnu-samhita; his disciple was Sriman Lakshmipati, the abode of the rasa of devotion; his disciple was Madhavendra, by whom this dharma was set in motion. He is the incarnation of the wish-fulfilling tree that grows in the abode of Vraja and bears the fruits called service, friendship, parental love and conjugal love.8

23His disciple was the renunciant Sriman Ishvara Puri, who, being the very fruit of conjugal love, manifested shringara.

24Advaita manifested both fruits, service and friendship; and Sriman Rangapuri took shelter in parental love.

25Gaura, accepting Ishvara Puri with reverence as His guru, flooded the world, both material and spiritual.

Gaura, "the devotee in form"

26Although He is Sri Nandanandana Himself, an ocean of rasa within and without, He accepted the mood and the lustre of Radhika, which had never before been attained.

27The original vyuha,9 whose mind was once stirred in His city on seeing the dance of the Gandharvas, also entered into Chaitanya.

28The Lord (Bhagavan) who dwells in Dvaraka also entered the son of Shachi, and so, by the power of simultaneity, did the many incarnations —

29just as once Shyama10 entered into Bhagavan Krishna Himself.

30Although by the power of Yogamaya they remain elsewhere as well, still they entered into Gaura — which is recognized only by inconceivable signs.

31As the feet of Vyasa have said in the Prabhasa-khanda: "Truths that are inconceivable must not be subjected to reasoning."

32As Bhargava,11 though he entered into Raghunatha, still remains separately, so Narada and the others remain in other abodes and at the same time sport with the Lord, like the personified shrutis.

33But whatever mood (bhava) the various devotees delighted in, in accordance with that mood they attained their destination in Vraja.

34As Gaura says to Advaita in the Gaura-chandrodaya:12 "Some are in service, some are loving in friendship, and some in both; some are devoted to Radha and Madhava, some to the Lord of Dvaraka; others in friendship and the rest towards both, and still others towards other incarnations — all of them, binding their hearts to Me, I shall make devoted to Vrindavana."

Mahaprabhu's relatives

35The cowherd named Parjanya, Krishna's grandfather, was born in Shrihatta as Upendra Mishra, the father of seven sons.

36The eminent cowherd woman of Vraja named Mahamanya, Krishna's grandmother, here bears the name Kamalavati.

37Yashoda and the king of Vraja, Nanda, who once in Vrindavana were mines of the rasa of love, became Shachi and Jagannatha Purandara — of this there is no doubt.

38Into them also entered the divine Aditi and Kashyapa, Sri Kaushalya and Dasharatha, and Sri Prishni and her husband.

39Some say that Devaki and Vasudeva, the parents of Rama and Krishna, entered into them too; otherwise Sri Vishvarupa, the form of Rama, could not have appeared.

40Rohini and Vasudeva, the parents of Rama and Krishna, were born as the best of brahmanas, Padmavati and Mukunda;13 into them also entered Sri Sumitra and Dasharatha.

41Paurnamasi, who brought joy to Govinda in Vraja, is the acharya Srila Govinda, the composer of songs and verses.

42The nurse in Vraja named Ambika, who once suckled Him, is this Malini, considered the wife of Srivasa.

43Ambika's sister, named Srila Kilimbika, who partook of Krishna's remnants, is considered to be Narayani.

44He who was once the great king Janaka, lord of Mithila, is now Vallabhacharya; he is also accepted as Bhishmaka.

45Sri Janaki and Rukmini are his daughter named Lakshmi; and so she is named Lakshmi in the Chaitanya-charita:

46"That daughter of Vallabhacharya, Lakshmi, incarnated for His sake, went with her friends to bathe in the river of the gods (the Ganga), and there came into the Lord's sight."

47Sri Sanatana Mishra is the former king Satrajit, whose daughter is Vishnupriya, the Mother of the world, the embodiment of Bhu.14

48This was said in passing by Kali in the Sri Chaitanya-chandrodaya: "…and having married another beloved, a partial manifestation of Bhu, known as Vishnupriya…" and so on.

49Vishvamitra, who was the matchmaker at Sri Rama's wedding, and the brahmana sent by Rukmini to Sri Keshava — these two are Vanamali, who by this very service attained the position of acharya.15

50And the brahmana sent by Satrajit to Madhava as matchmaker for Satya's wedding is Sri Kashinatha.

51By a certain secondary distinction, the Satvatas hold that Jagadananda Pandita is a manifestation of Satyabhama.

52The sage Sandipani, who once in Mathura gave Krishna the sacred thread, has now become Keshava Bharati.

53The sage Vasishtha, once the guru of Raghunatha, became by a special manifestation Gangadasa and Sudarshana.16

54He who was once famous in the land of Vraja as Vrishabhanu is now the venerable Pundarika Vidyanidhi.

55Tasting His own mood and afflicted by separation like Radha, Chaitanya Himself called Pundarika "Father."

56Gaura joyfully gave him the glorious name Premanidhi, and always honoured him, because he was a disciple of Madhavendra.

57A special manifestation of him is considered to be Sri Madhava Mishra,17 and his wife Ratnavati is declared by the wise to be Kirtida.

✦

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. Srinatha Pandita, the guru of Kavi Karnapura, a disciple of Advaita Acharya.
  2. That is, the five truths are not separate from Krishna: were they not bound to Him by oneness, there would be a set of four truths separate from Him.
  3. Svarupa Damodara, Chaitanya's closest associate in Puri. His Kadacha (notes), on which Kavi Karnapura draws, has not come down to us; it is known only through quotations.
  4. Halayudha ("armed with the plough") is Balarama.
  5. The twelve gopalas of Nityananda and the upa-gopalas are the traditional grouping of His associates.
  6. Nrihari: Hari appearing as a man.
  7. Shatadushani ("A Hundred Refutations") is apparently the traditional name of a polemical compendium against Advaita (monism).
  8. This "Madhva" succession of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas (through Lakshmipati to Madhavendra Puri) is one of the most discussed passages of the book; some scholars consider it a later interpolation.
  9. The original vyuha is Vasudeva, the first of the four vyuhas (Vasudeva, Sankarshana, Pradyumna, Aniruddha).
  10. Shyama is the yuga-avatara of the Dvapara age.
  11. Bhargava is Parashurama.
  12. That is, the Chaitanya-chandrodaya, the drama by Kavi Karnapura himself (Act 10).
  13. The parents of Nityananda.
  14. Bhu is Bhumi, the goddess Earth, one of the consorts of Vishnu.
  15. Vanamali Acharya, who arranged the marriage of Nimai and Lakshmipriya.
  16. Gangadasa and Sudarshana were the teachers of the young Nimai.
  17. The father of Gadadhara Pandita.
